# AgentPresence

The person's always-visible sign of which of their agents are listening to something on their behalf, such as a meeting, with Stop one click away. A chip with the agent sparkle says "inbox agent listening", or "2 agents listening"; it opens a popover that lists each agent, what it listens for and a Stop, plus Stop all with two or more. It never hides itself while an agent listens (no fading, no collapsing), and renders nothing when none does. `compact` shows only the sparkle and a count, and `unread` a dot when an agent left something for the person.

```tsx
import { AgentPresence } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/agent-presence/agent-presence";
```

## Example

```tsx
<AgentPresence
  label="Agents listening"
  agents={[{ id: "inbox", name: "inbox agent", doing: "listening for your name" }]}
  onStop={(id) => stopListening(id)}
/>
<AgentPresence label="Agents listening" agents={agents} onStop={stop} onStopAll={stopAll} compact unread />
```

## Usage

The chip is a button named by the count and the names ("2 agents listening: inbox agent, research agent"). When an agent starts or stops listening, screen readers hear it once, politely ("inbox agent is now listening", "inbox agent stopped"). When a Stop goes with its agent, focus moves to the next Stop, and when the last agent goes, to the control after the chip.

Its agent side, `agentPresenceAx` in `agent-presence-styles.ts`, lets agents read who is listening and what for (consent `none`), and take Stop and Stop all, since stopping only reduces what is heard. It offers no way to start listening: that stays the person's.

## Use instead when

- Use `Avatar` or `Badge` instead to show who is present in a conversation, and `toast()` for a one-off notice.

## Props

Type: `AgentPresenceProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agents` (required) | `readonly ListeningAgent[]` |  | The agents listening now. With none, AgentPresence renders nothing; keep it mounted, so it can say when an agent stops or starts. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, placement (`ms-auto`). Appearance classes warn in development; use `size`. |
| `compact` | `boolean` |  | Only the sparkle and a count, for a tight bar or a floating mini-window. Its name still says who is listening. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Names the list of agents: the popover's title, "Agents listening". It is always required. |
| `labels` | `AgentPresenceLabels` |  | The words it says, for other languages. |
| `onStop` (required) | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with an agent's `id` when the person presses its Stop. Stop the agent and drop it from `agents`; AgentPresence says "inbox agent stopped" once it has gone. |
| `onStopAll` | `(() => void)` |  | Called when the person presses Stop all, which shows with two agents or more. Without it, Stop all calls `onStop` for each agent. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"sm"` | The chip's size, Button's sizes. |
| `unread` | `boolean` |  | Shows a dot on the chip: an agent left something for the person. AgentPresence opens nothing for it; the app shows what was left where it belongs. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `autoHide`: Not a prop. AgentPresence never hides while an agent listens; it renders nothing only when `agents` is empty.
- `listeners`: Not a prop. The agents are `agents`: `<AgentPresence agents={[{ id: "inbox", name: "inbox agent" }]}>`.
- `onRemove`: Not a prop. Ouro UI says `onStop`, called with the agent's id: `<AgentPresence onStop={(id) => stop(id)}>`.
- `variant`: Not a prop. The small form is `compact`: `<AgentPresence compact>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `AgentPresenceLabels`

The words AgentPresence says, for apps in other languages.

```ts
interface AgentPresenceLabels {
  /** The chip for one agent. @default (name) => `${name} listening` */
  one?: ((name: string) => string) | undefined;
  /** The chip for several. @default (count) => `${count} agents listening` */
  many?: ((count: number) => string) | undefined;
  /** Said once when an agent starts listening. @default (name) => `${name} is now listening` */
  started?: ((name: string) => string) | undefined;
  /** Said once when an agent stops, whoever stopped it. @default (name) => `${name} stopped` */
  stopped?: ((name: string) => string) | undefined;
  /**
   * Each agent's Stop button. Screen readers hear the agent's name after it. @default "Stop"
   */
  stop?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * The button that stops every agent. @default "Stop all"
   */
  stopAll?: string | undefined;
  /** What screen readers hear for the unread dot. @default "Something new from your agents" */
  unread?: string | undefined;
  /** The popover's close button, which shows when it has keyboard focus. @default "Close" */
  close?: string | undefined;
}
```

### `ListeningAgent`

One agent listening for the person.

```ts
interface ListeningAgent {
  /** Stays the same while the agent listens; `onStop` gets it back. */
  id: string;
  /** What the person calls the agent, by its role: "inbox agent". */
  name: string;
  /** What it listens for, in a few words: "listening for your name, and anything about the empty state". */
  doing?: string | undefined;
}
```
